# @codenhub/jwt

> JwtKit: JSON Web Token signing, verification, encryption and decryption on Web Crypto, for tokens that must be treated as untrusted, with key generation, import and export, key sets, remote JWKS, key rotation, DPoP proofs, and JWS of any payload. Signs and verifies ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA, Ed25519, RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, HS256, HS384 and HS512; `none` is never accepted. Encrypts compact JWE with dir, A128KW, A256KW, ECDH-ES (+A128KW, +A256KW) on P-256, P-384, P-521 and X25519, RSA-OAEP-256 and RSA-OAEP, and A128GCM, A256GCM, A128CBC-HS256 and A256CBC-HS512. No runtime dependencies; runs on Node.js 26 or newer, browsers and edge runtimes. The package is experimental.

Every key is bound to exactly one algorithm when it is generated (`generateKeyPair`, `generateSecretKey`) or imported (`importPublicKey`, `importPrivateKey`, `importKeyPair`, `importSecretKey`, from a JWK, a PEM in SPKI, PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC 1 or a certificate, or a Web Crypto `CryptoKey`); a token verifies only with a key whose `alg` equals its header's `alg`. Keys are opaque frozen objects (`kind` is `public`, `private` or `secret`); only objects this package created are accepted, and only by the same copy of the package, so a program must load one copy (dedupe the install; a library built on it declares it as a `peerDependency`). `kid: "thumbprint"` names a key by its RFC 7638 thumbprint; `jwkThumbprint`, `jwkThumbprintUri` and `certificateThumbprint` compute thumbprints, and `exportPublicJwk`, `exportPrivateJwk`, `exportSecretJwk`, `exportPublicPem` and `exportPrivatePem` export keys. `createExternalSigningKey` signs with a key held by a KMS or HSM.

`createVerifier({ keys, issuer, subject, audience, type, requireExpiration, allowExpired, clockTolerance, maxAge, maxLength, requiredClaims, claims, now, onKeySetError })` returns `verify(token)`, which resolves to `{ ok: true, value: { header, payload, key } }` or `{ ok: false, error: { issues } }` and never throws for a token; only a `claims` schema that throws or rejects makes it reject. A token without `exp`, or with an `aud` when no `audience` is set, fails unless waived. Durations are seconds; `now` returns milliseconds. Checks run in order: length cap (default 8192), strict base64url and JSON (duplicate keys rejected, depth 32), supported `alg`, no `crit`, key selection, signature, then claims (all claim failures reported together), then the optional Standard Schema `claims`. There is no unverified payload decode; `readHeader(token)` returns only the header. `sign({ payload, key, header, issuedAt, notBefore, expiresIn, jti, now })` takes `alg` from the key and adds only the claims its options ask for.

Key sets: `createKeySet(keys)`, `importKeySet(jwks, { algorithms, issuer })`, `createRemoteKeySet({ url, fetch, algorithms, issuer, cacheTtl, cooldown, maxStale, timeout, maxResponseBytes, now, seed, onFetch, onFetchError, waitUntil })` for an https JWKS URL with caching that honours `max-age`, a refetch on unknown `kid` limited by a cooldown, and stale keys while the issuer is unreachable, and a `keys` function from the claimed `iss` to a key set or route. Selection never tries keys in turn. `createKeyRing` schedules an issuer's signing keys and publishes its JWKS. `createDpopProof` and `createDpopVerifier` create and check RFC 9449 DPoP proofs. `signJws`, `signGeneralJws` and `createJwsVerifier` handle a JWS of any payload, compact or JSON, with RFC 7797 unencoded and detached payloads.

Encryption keys are separate kinds (`generateJweKeyPair`, `generateJweSecretKey`, `importJwePublicKey`, `importJwePrivateKey`, `importJweKeyPair`, `importJweSecretKey`), bound to one key management algorithm. `encrypt` and `createDecrypter` handle any payload as bytes; `encryptJwt` signs then encrypts and `createNestedVerifier` decrypts then verifies. Every failure after key selection is `decryption_failed`; `RSA1_5`, `PBES2`, `zip` and `crit` are refused. Issues have a stable `code`, optional `path` and `params`, and the package's own issues never contain input values; a `claims` schema's path may name payload properties, and a custom key set's issues are passed through. Invalid options and foreign key objects throw `TypeError`.

## Documentation

- [Documentation overview](docs/index.md): What a JWT is, algorithm binding, the result shape, the check order, encrypted tokens, and requirements.
- [Verifying tokens](docs/verifying.md): Every `createVerifier` option, check order, time claims and clock tolerance, issuer, subject, audience and `typ` matching, Standard Schema claims, and `readHeader`.
- [Signing tokens](docs/signing.md): What `sign` writes into the header, refused header parameters, the payload rules, the claims it adds when asked, and token hashes.
- [Keys](docs/keys.md): Key kinds, generating, importing JWKs, PEM, Web Crypto keys and raw secrets with the checks and issues of each, KMS and HSM keys, exporting, and thumbprints.
- [Key sets](docs/key-sets.md): Selection rules, local sets, importing a JWKS, choosing a key set by issuer, and remote JWKS caching, cooldown, stale keys and fetch failures.
- [Key rotation](docs/rotation.md): Rotating an issuer's signing keys with `createKeyRing`, publishing each key before and after it signs, and replacing a leaked key.
- [DPoP proofs](docs/dpop.md): Creating and verifying RFC 9449 proofs, access token binding, nonces and replay checks.
- [Encrypting tokens](docs/encrypting.md): Compact JWE encryption and decryption, encryption keys and algorithms, signed tokens inside encrypted ones, and a recipient's encryption JWKS.
- [JWS](docs/jws.md): Signing and verifying any payload in the compact or JSON serialization, with unencoded and detached payloads.
- [Issues](docs/errors.md): The result shape and every issue code with its path and params, and what throws instead.
